partition_policy.training: all target facts except source-exclusive validation and blind facts

results.name: Affected disease-associated gene baseline
results.hypothesis: A chemical that affects a gene associated with a disease may treat that disease.
results.mechanism_rationale: Connects a chemical to a disease-linked gene, but does not require a therapeutically corrective direction or corroborating mechanism.
results.trapi_notes: A two-edge TRAPI query can express the graph pattern; edge-property refinements would require constraints.

results.name: Direct target with disease-gene association baseline
results.hypothesis: A chemical that directly physically interacts with a disease-associated gene may treat the disease.
results.mechanism_rationale: Direct molecular interaction is stronger than generic affects, but the rule lacks direction, functional consequence, and pathway corroboration.
results.trapi_notes: The two-edge path is directly expressible in TRAPI.

results.name: Selective inhibition of a causal disease gene
results.hypothesis: A chemical may treat a disease when it selectively decreases the activity or abundance of a gene asserted to cause the disease.
results.body: chemical -affects[causes, activity_or_abundance, decreased]-> causal gene -causes-> disease; chemical qualified gene degree <=50
results.mechanism_rationale: The chemical perturbation direction opposes a causal disease gene, and the degree constraint removes broad perturbagens.
results.trapi_notes: The path and edge qualifiers are TRAPI-expressible; the chemical degree constraint requires Cypher or post-processing.

results.name: Multi-gene inhibition within a disease-supported process
results.hypothesis: A selective chemical may treat a disease when it decreases multiple disease-associated genes participating in the same bounded-size biological process.
results.body: disease has 3-20 associated genes in a process; chemical decreases activity_or_abundance of >=2 of those genes; chemical qualified gene degree <=100
results.mechanism_rationale: Requires directional perturbation of multiple disease genes in a coherent process and explicitly suppresses chemical and process hubs.
results.trapi_notes: The graph motif and qualifiers are TRAPI-expressible; cardinality and degree constraints require Cypher or post-processing.

results.name: Normalized phenotype indication transfer
results.hypothesis: A treatment for one disease may transfer to another disease when at least half of the smaller disease phenotype profile is shared and both profiles are bounded.
results.body: chemical -treats-> anchor disease; anchor and candidate disease share >=3 phenotypes; shared/min(phenotype degrees) >=0.5; each phenotype degree 3-50
results.mechanism_rationale: Phenotypic similarity supports indication transfer but does not identify the drug mechanism responsible for efficacy.
results.trapi_notes: The graph pattern is TRAPI-expressible; normalized overlap, degree limits, and source exclusion require post-processing or Cypher.

results.name: Normalized genetic indication transfer
results.hypothesis: A treatment for one disease may transfer to another disease when the diseases share multiple associated genes and at least half of the smaller gene profile.
results.body: chemical -treats-> anchor disease; anchor and candidate disease share >=2 associated genes; shared/min(gene degrees) >=0.5; each gene degree 2-100
results.mechanism_rationale: Genetic similarity provides a disease-mechanism bridge, but efficacy is still transferred from an existing indication.
results.trapi_notes: The graph pattern is TRAPI-expressible; normalized overlap, degree limits, and source exclusion require post-processing or Cypher.

results.name: Clinical-trial evidence benchmark
results.hypothesis: A chemical tested in clinical trials for a disease is enriched for exact treats assertions.
results.mechanism_rationale: This is direct treatment-development evidence rather than an explanatory biological mechanism.
results.trapi_notes: A one-edge TRAPI query expresses the rule.

results.name: Studied-to-treat evidence benchmark
results.hypothesis: A chemical studied to treat a disease is enriched for exact treats assertions.
results.mechanism_rationale: The rule restates treatment study evidence and does not explain efficacy.
results.trapi_notes: A one-edge TRAPI query expresses the rule.

results.name: Applied-to-treat evidence benchmark
results.hypothesis: A chemical applied to treat a disease is enriched for exact treats assertions.
results.mechanism_rationale: This is treatment-use evidence rather than a mechanistic explanation.
results.trapi_notes: A one-edge TRAPI query expresses the rule.

results.name: Direct binding plus inhibition of a causal gene
results.hypothesis: A chemical may treat a disease when it both directly binds and decreases the activity or abundance of a causal disease gene.
results.body: chemical -directly_physically_interacts_with-> causal gene -causes-> disease; same chemical -affects[causes, activity_or_abundance, decreased]-> same gene; qualified gene degree <=50
results.mechanism_rationale: Requires target engagement, a directionally corrective perturbation, and a causal disease link on the same gene.
results.trapi_notes: The parallel-edge motif and qualifiers are TRAPI-expressible; the degree constraint requires Cypher or post-processing.

results.name: Tight multi-gene inhibition in a compact disease process
results.hypothesis: Precision improves when a selective chemical decreases at least three disease-associated genes in a compact process.
results.body: disease has 3-10 associated genes in a process; chemical decreases activity_or_abundance of >=3; chemical qualified gene degree <=50
results.mechanism_rationale: This is a stricter, hub-resistant form of multi-target pathway correction.
results.trapi_notes: The graph motif and qualifiers are TRAPI-expressible; cardinality and degree constraints require Cypher or post-processing.
